note: Assumptions for the I/O and power estimate shown on the console while Left Alt is held (panels/virtual/budget.js). Rough figures, to compare modules and see which board a grouping overloads; change them as the parts are chosen.

olimex-esp32-poe2.name: Olimex ESP32-POE2
olimex-esp32-poe2.note: the 5 V rail: 1.5 A (7.5 W) for the display drivers and lamps. The board's 25 W from PoE (802.3at) is split: 5 V 1.5 A, 3.3 V 1 A (the ESP32 and Ethernet, counted apart), and 12 V 1.5 A or 24 V 0.75 A by jumper; logic_w: the ESP32 and Ethernet on the 3.3 V rail, in the PoE total but not against the 5 V limit

olimex-esp32-poe.name: Olimex ESP32-POE
olimex-esp32-poe.note: 4 W (0.8 A at 5 V, the 3.3 V rail included) from PoE, per Olimex; the ESP32 with Ethernet takes about 0.75 W of it

raspberry-pi.name: Raspberry Pi
raspberry-pi.note: a glass module: the Pi and its screen have their own supply; only the panel's I/O is counted

mcp23017.note: I2C expander: switches, buttons, rotary positions, keypad lines, lamps

max7219.note: 8 rows of 8 LEDs: a 7-segment digit per row, or 8 bar segments or matrix dots; 20 mA segments (RSET), 160 mA with every segment lit, about 32 mA with 40 % lit at half intensity

lamps.note: led_ma: a 5 mm indicator LED; lamp_ma: a lit push button or an annunciator cell; typical_on: the share of lamps lit in flight

pins.note: ESP32 pins: the shared I2C bus, the MAX7219 chain, a buzzer on its own PWM pin
